body.x: Gbrain (Co-CEOs Sunggu Yang and Byoung Kim) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

As a pioneering company in the Korean neurotechnology market, Gbrain leads advancements in brain-computer interface (BCI) medical solutions. It is the first in Korea to commercialize invasive electrodes and holds unparalleled expertise in designing and manufacturing flexible, noninvasive thin-film electrodes for high-resolution brainwave acquisition. According to company representatives, these electrodes are designed to attach to the brain cortex, minimizing tissue damage and adapting seamlessly to the brain's curvature. They enable stable and efficient acquisition of high-quality brainwave data.

Gbrain’s innovative technologies are opening new possibilities in neuroscience and medicine, garnering attention in global markets. Notably, Gbrain’s excellence was recognized as an Honoree in the Digital Health category of the highly competitive CES Innovation Awards.

At CES 2025, Gbrain introduced Phin Stim, a cortical monitoring and stimulation implant system that provides a groundbreaking treatment option for patients with intractable brain diseases, such as Parkinson's and epilepsy. This solution offers an alternative to traditional drug therapies or surgical treatments.

body.cap: Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter, interviews Sunggu Yang, Co-CEO of Gbrain | Photo by AVING News

body.x: A Gbrain representative explained, "Current treatments for intractable brain diseases typically involve deeply invasive electrode therapies or cortical monitoring/stimulation techniques that require a seven-day hospital stay with direct connection of brain electrodes to computers via wires, significantly limiting mobility. Gbrain’s Phin Stim overcomes these challenges by minimizing brain tissue invasion and employing wireless communication technology, making it the first domestic attempt to commercialize this innovative approach."

The representative further noted, "Led by Sunggu Yang, a professor of Nano-Bioengineering at Incheon University, and Byoung Kim, a former executive at Celltrion, Gbrain’s board includes electronics, neuro-engineering, and materials science experts. Together, they are advancing interdisciplinary and integrative BCI technology solutions."

Gbrain also shared its plans. In the short term, the company aims to solidify its position as Korea’s first to develop minimally invasive electrode solutions for treating intractable brain diseases. In the medium and long term, it plans to integrate IoT and AI technologies to enable brainwave-based control and communication with surrounding objects, pushing the boundaries of BCI technology.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
